newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's SABIC seeks to sell MTBE to Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's SABIC seeks to sell MTBE to Egypt.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) is seeking to sell more MTBE to Egypt and plans to set up a marketing office in Cairo to help boost trade, the company said on Monday.

A company statement said SABIC's Vice-Chairman Ibrahim bin Salameh arrived in Egypt "to sign new contracts with the Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) concerning methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE)".
SABIC last year won a contract to supply 230,000 tonnes of MTBE to Egypt, of which 70,000 tonnes had been shipped in 1996 and the remainder would be delivered this year.

SABIC, which accounts for around five percent of the world's petrochemical output, currently produces more than 2.7 million tonnes a year of MTBE, an additive which makes gasoline burn Salameh said the Egyptian market was growing and that SABIC had sold 583,000 tonnes of petrochemical products to Egypt in 1996, up from 34,000 tonnes in 1991.
He said he would also discuss opening a company or an office called 'SABIC Misr' to help boost marketing in the region.
"The good investment environment provided by the two countries' governments (Egypt and Saudi Arabia) affirms the importance to set up joint industrial projects," he said.
SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, also said it planned to open an office in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Salameh described UAE markets as promising and said the move would help supply products to increasing numbers of customers there.
